run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 13 of the usual 15 holdings. ASML Holding and Glencore plc weren't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the companies themselves.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down a bit and now sits well off its high from last year, but defense budgets are still growing steadily, so nothing has really changed about the underlying business.

ASML.sentence: ASML Holding didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet day — industrial gas demand is steady and they keep nudging prices up a little each quarter, which is the whole story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet and holding up better than most of its tech peers lately — the Azure cloud and AI story keeps grinding along without much drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is sitting near its highs and barely moved — the rough patch for lab-equipment buyers looks mostly behind it now.

CVX.sentence: Chevron ticked up with oil prices, which are unusually high right now because fighting involving Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments — so its profits are swollen by the oil price rather than anything the company itself did.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced a little today but is still way down from its high, even as big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its AI workflow tools under long-term contracts — a case where the share price has fallen further than the business.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore plc didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta slipped slightly, but the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up faster than its costs — the part that actually matters — so the business is intact.

KOF.sentence: The Mexican Coca-Cola bottler had a nice up day, though a weakening peso is a mild headwind since most of its sales are earned in pesos and worth a bit less in dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber edged up, and people keep booking more rides and food orders than ever with no sign robotaxi companies are pulling their cars off the app — so the self-driving question is still about the future, not today's business.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk rose a bit, and you can currently buy its fleet of ships for well below what it would cost to build them — a sign the stock is priced cheaply against its actual assets.

MA.sentence: Mastercard had a good day, and people keep tapping their cards more than ever — the tiny toll it collects on every transaction remains a remarkably steady business.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company had a good day and is down meaningfully from its high even as hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines — and every procedure means more disposable supplies sold, which is where most of their money comes from.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell again after Google's parent and Amazon showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the difference — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are the customers whose wallets pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
